Dust maps preserve statistical correlation with HI column density maps. The spatial variations in dust emission relative to hydrogen column density are characterized as a function of angular scale.
AI.conclusion: The WPH-based component-separation algorithm effectively extracts Galactic dust emission from CIB-dominated regions at Planck 353 GHz, providing a validated alternative to the standard template-fit approach and enabling analysis of dust-HI correlations across angular scales.

title: Stellar mass growth in COSMOS-Web: a mass-complete main sequence to z ~ 8 and its consistency with GSMF evolution
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: The star-forming main sequence (MS) links the instantaneous star-formation rate of galaxies to their stellar-mass growth and therefore to the evolution of the galaxy stellar mass function (GSMF). We determine a mass-complete MS in COSMOS-Web out to z=8 and test whether its mass and redshift dependence is consistent with the observed evolution of the GSMF. We stacked 251,462 star-forming galaxies in Herschel and JCMT maps and corrected the far-infrared fluxes for blending using forward-modeled maps. We combined the resulting infrared luminosities with the unobscured ultraviolet emission to derive total star-formation rates and fitted a redshift-dependent MS. We independently measured the quiescent fraction and evolved the observed z=8 COSMOS-Web GSMF forward within a continuity-equation framework including stellar-mass return, suppression of in-situ growth by the quiescent fraction, and mergers. The MS is well described by a power law at low masses with a redshift-dependent turnover toward high masses. We measure a low-mass slope of gamma=1.215+/-0.028, implying a mildly increasing specific star-formation rate with stellar mass. The GSMF evolved using this relation follows the observed progressive flattening of the low-mass end substantially better than the literature MS prescriptions considered here. Mergers change the low-mass number densities by <=0.2 dex by z~0.65 and have little effect on the slope. Small differences in MS normalization also accumulate strongly, producing large differences in the evolved GSMF after several Gyr. The observed GSMF evolution provides an independent integral test of the MS. Our results favor a mildly super-linear low-mass MS and show that both its slope and normalization must be measured accurately to reproduce the buildup of the galaxy stellar-mass distribution.

AI.tldr: This study uses COSMOS-Web data out to z=8 to determine a mass-complete star-forming main sequence (MS) from 251,462 stacked galaxies using Herschel and JCMT far-infrared/submillimeter data. The authors find a power-law MS at low masses with a redshift-dependent turnover (slope γ=1.215±0.028), and show that evolving the z=8 GSMF forward via continuity equations with this MS reproduces the observed low-mass flattening of the GSMF better than literature prescriptions. They conclude that the MS slope and normalization must both be measured accurately to reproduce galaxy stellar-mass assembly.
AI.motivation: To test whether the mass and redshift dependence of the star-forming main sequence is consistent with the observed evolution of the galaxy stellar mass function, providing a direct integral test of the MS against independent observations.
AI.method: The authors stacked 251,462 star-forming galaxies in Herschel and JCMT maps, corrected far-infrared fluxes for blending using forward-modeled maps, combined infrared and unobscured ultraviolet luminosities to derive total SFRs, fitted a redshift-dependent MS, and evolved the observed z=8 COSMOS-Web GSMF forward within a continuity-equation framework including stellar-mass return, quiescent fraction suppression, and mergers.
AI.result: The MS is described by a low-mass power law with slope γ=1.215±0.028 and a redshift-dependent high-mass turnover. The evolved GSMF matches the observed progressive flattening of the low-mass end substantially better than literature MS prescriptions. Mergers affect low-mass number densities by ≤0.2 dex by z~0.65, while small differences in MS normalization accumulate strongly over time.
AI.conclusion: The observed GSMF evolution independently validates the derived MS relation, favoring a mildly super-linear low-mass MS. Both the slope and normalization of the MS must be accurately measured to reproduce the buildup of the galaxy stellar-mass distribution.

title: Evidence for the transformation from lenticular to spiral galaxies
comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, 1 table, submitted to ApJ
summary: It is widely accepted that late-type galaxies, such as spirals, evolve into early-type systems, including elliptical and lenticular galaxies, through galaxy mergers and violent disk instability processes. Throughout this morphological transformation, star formation is typically suppressed by quenching mechanisms whose detailed nature remains the subject of active investigation. Here, we present compelling evidence for an evolutionary pathway that proceeds in the reverse direction. Using the integral field unit observations, we identify a population of spiral galaxies hosting quenched central cores (QCCs). These galaxies exhibit bimodal distributions in both their stellar population properties and their dynamical properties, along with sharp changes in radial gradients near the QCC boundary. These results indicate that the QCCs and the surrounding outer disks formed at distinct cosmic epochs and through different physical processes. Remarkably, QCCs closely resemble quiescent early-type galaxies, particularly lenticular galaxies, in their mass-size and mass-velocity dispersion scaling relations, as well as in their stellar population demographics and internal kinematics. These findings provide strong support for a rejuvenation scenario in which spiral disks are reassembled around pre-existing quiescent lenticular or early-type systems. Moreover, we show that such rejuvenation, accompanied by a reverse morphological transformation from early- to late-type appearance, is quite common. This indicates that quenching in galaxies is not invariably a terminal state and can be reversed under appropriate conditions.

AI.tldr: Using integral field unit observations, this paper identifies spiral galaxies with quenched central cores (QCCs) that resemble lenticular/early-type galaxies, providing evidence for a reverse morphological transformation where spiral disks are reassembled around pre-existing quiescent early-type systems, indicating that quenching is not always a terminal state.
AI.motivation: The standard paradigm holds that late-type galaxies evolve into early-type galaxies via mergers and disk instabilities, with star formation suppressed by quenching. However, the reverse pathway—early-type galaxies being rejuvenated into late-type spirals—remains underexplored. The authors aim to find observational evidence for such reverse morphological transformation.
AI.method: The study uses integral field unit (IFU) observations to identify a population of spiral galaxies hosting quenched central cores (QCCs). They analyze stellar population properties, dynamical properties, and radial gradients, comparing QCCs against early-type galaxies (particularly lenticulars) in mass-size and mass-velocity dispersion scaling relations, as well as stellar population demographics and internal kinematics.
AI.result: The QCC-hosting spirals exhibit bimodal distributions in stellar population and dynamical properties, with sharp radial gradient changes at the QCC boundary, suggesting distinct formation epochs and mechanisms for the cores versus outer disks. QCCs closely match quiescent lenticular/early-type galaxies in scaling relations and population demographics. The reverse transformation (early- to late-type) appears common.
AI.conclusion: The findings support a rejuvenation scenario where spiral disks are reassembled around pre-existing quiescent early-type cores. Quenching is not always a terminal, irreversible state—galaxies can be rejuvenated under appropriate conditions, and such reverse morphological transformations are common.

title: Formation of Accretion Disks around Intermediate-Mass Black Holes in Ultra Compact Dwarf Galaxies and Nuclear Stellar Clusters
comment: 22 pages, 26 figures
summary: Recent observations have found many ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs) that contain massive black holes (MBHs) typically consisting of $10\%-15\%$ of their total mass, with some as high as $40\%$. However, whether UCDs initially started with MBHs or grew from intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) is unclear. We propose a mechanism in which AGB stars have their gas ejected which forms an accretion disk around an IMBH to fuel BH growth. We used smooth particle hydrodynamical simulations to (i) model the creation and evolution of gas disks that can finally evolve into accretion disks and to investigate (ii) how the properties of the gas disk depend on the model. We find that the amount of mass in the disk increases more with UCD mass than with IMBH mass. For lower-mass IMBHs of $100 \text{ M}_\odot$, a majority of the gas mass present can be trapped in a disk, leading to the idea that lower-mass BHs can utilise the proposed mechanism. The main mechanism working against accretion disk formation is the creation of new stars within the disk, not just through the removal of gas but through gravitational disruption as well. Finally, an estimation of the total BH growth provides a list of observed UCDs which could have formed MBHs using the proposed mechanism which can be useful for verifying the proposed mechanism. Future simulations aimed at modelling the formation of such UCDs can be employed to provide a full picture of the results presented in this paper.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism where asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars in ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs) eject gas that forms accretion disks around intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs), fueling their growth into massive black holes (MBHs). Using smooth particle hydrodynamical simulations, the authors find that disk mass increases more with UCD mass than IMBH mass, lower-mass IMBHs can efficiently trap gas, and star formation within the disk is the primary obstacle. They also identify observed UCDs where this mechanism could have produced MBHs.
AI.motivation: Recent observations reveal ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs) containing massive black holes (MBHs) comprising 10-40% of their total mass, but it is unclear whether these MBHs originated initially or grew from intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs). The paper aims to address this open question by proposing and testing a mechanism for IMBH growth in UCDs.
AI.method: The authors use smooth particle hydrodynamical (SPH) simulations to (i) model the creation and evolution of gas disks that can eventually evolve into accretion disks around IMBHs, and (ii) investigate how disk properties depend on model parameters such as UCD mass and IMBH mass.
AI.result: The simulations show that the amount of disk mass increases more strongly with UCD mass than with IMBH mass. For lower-mass IMBHs (100 M_sun), a majority of the available gas mass can be trapped in a disk, enabling the proposed mechanism. The main barrier to accretion disk formation is star formation within the disk, which both removes gas and disrupts the disk gravitationally. The authors also provide an estimate of total BH growth and identify observed UCDs that could have formed MBHs via this mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The proposed AGB-star gas ejection mechanism is a viable pathway for IMBH growth into MBHs in UCDs, particularly for lower-mass IMBHs. A list of observed UCDs potentially formed through this mechanism is provided for observational verification, and future simulations modelling UCD formation could provide a more complete picture.

title: HII-CHI-mistry for active galactic nuclei: optical sulphur abundances without empirical ionisation correction factors
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures. To be submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: > The determination of sulphur abundances in active galactic nuclei (AGN) is uncertain because ionisation correction factors (ICFs) are commonly calibrated for HII regions. We extend the HII-CHI-mistry methodology to derive total S/H in AGN from optical emission lines through comparison with photoionisation models. Tests against Seyfert galaxies with direct-method ionic abundances favour models with alpha_ox=-1.2 and a 98% free-electron stopping criterion. While O/H agrees with previous determinations, HCm yields systematically larger S/H than direct-method analyses using classical ICFs, suggesting that these prescriptions underestimate higher sulphur ionisation stages in AGN. Applied to MaNGA Seyfert and LINER-like regions, the method reveals a common positive S/O-metallicity relation. Seyferts show slightly larger median S/O than star-forming regions at high O/H, while LINERs occupy an intermediate position. These differences become weaker when S/H rather than O/H is used as the metallicity tracer, although Seyferts still tend to populate the upper envelope. Sulphur may therefore provide a robust tracer of gas-phase metallicity, while the differences between Seyferts and LINERs may reflect differences in their ionisation conditions and ionising SEDs.

Applied to MaNGA Seyferts and LINERs, the method reveals a common positive S/O-metallicity relation, with sulphur proposed as a robust tracer of gas-phase metallicity.
AI.motivation: Sulphur abundance determinations in AGN are uncertain because ionisation correction factors (ICFs) are commonly calibrated for HII regions rather than AGN environments, where the ionising conditions differ.
AI.method: The authors extend the HII-CHI-mistry methodology to derive total S/H in AGN from optical emission lines by comparing with photoionisation models. They test their models against Seyfert galaxies with direct-method ionic abundances, favouring models with alpha_ox=-1.2 and a 98% free-electron stopping criterion.
AI.result: O/H agrees with previous determinations, but HCm yields systematically larger S/H than direct-method analyses using classical ICFs, suggesting these prescriptions underestimate higher sulphur ionisation stages in AGN. Applied to MaNGA Seyfert and LINER-like regions, the method reveals a common positive S/O-metallicity relation. Seyferts show slightly larger median S/O than star-forming regions at high O/H, while LINERs occupy an intermediate position.

title: REBELS-25: multi-phase morphology and kinematics at z = 7.31
comment: 28 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present a spatially resolved, multi-wavelength study of the massive, star-forming galaxy REBELS-25 at a redshift of $z=7.31$. We combine new high-resolution ALMA [O III]88$μ$m observations with resolution-matched [C II], dust continuum, and JWST/NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy, providing a $\lesssim1$ kpc view of the morphology, interstellar medium (ISM) conditions, and multi-tracer gas kinematics of one of the most mature galaxies known in the reionisation era. We find differing morphologies from the rest-frame UV to far-infrared (FIR) emission, with the UV and optical emission appearing clumpy and irregular, whereas the FIR emission is well-described by near-exponential disc profiles, with [C II] being the most extended. Comparing the resolved UV and FIR emission, we find that obscured star formation contributes $\sim55$-$98$% of the total star formation rate across the galaxy, demonstrating that dust obscuration strongly shapes the observed UV and optical morphology. Resolved ionisation-line diagnostics show no significant variation across the source at $\sim1$ kpc resolution, consistent with broadly similar ISM conditions among the identified regions. Kinematic modelling reveals that both the warm ionised gas, traced by [O III]88$μ$m, and the colder neutral gas, traced by [C II], share the same large-scale rotating structure and are dynamically cold, with ratios of ordered-to-random motion, $V/σ$, of $\sim11$ and 4.5, respectively, although we find evidence for non-circular motions that are not well-described by a simple rotating disc. Overall, these results further support a picture in which REBELS-25 hosts a dusty, chemically enriched, and dynamically cold ISM already in place at $z=7.31$.

AI.tldr: Spatially resolved multi-wavelength study (ALMA [O III], [C II], dust continuum; JWST/NIRSpec IFU) of massive star-forming galaxy REBELS-25 at z=7.31 reveals clumpy UV/optical emission versus exponential FIR disc profiles, 55-98% obscured star formation fraction, uniform ISM conditions at ~1 kpc scales, and dynamically cold rotating gas (V/σ ~11 for ionized, 4.5 for neutral) with evidence of non-circular motions.
AI.motivation: To characterize the resolved morphology, ISM conditions, and multi-tracer kinematics of one of the most mature galaxies in the reionisation era, testing whether a dynamically cold and dusty ISM can already exist at z~7.3.
AI.method: Combines new high-resolution ALMA [O III]88μm observations with resolution-matched [C II], dust continuum, and JWST/NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy to achieve <1 kpc spatial resolution. Uses morphology fitting (UV-to-FIR comparison), resolved ionisation-line diagnostics, and kinematic modelling of rotating disc components with ordered-to-random motion ratios.
AI.result: UV/optical emission is clumpy and irregular while FIR emission follows near-exponential disc profiles with [C II] most extended; obscured star formation contributes ~55-98% of total SFR; ionisation diagnostics show no significant spatial variation at ~1 kpc; both [O III] and [C II] trace the same large-scale rotation with V/σ ~11 and 4.5 respectively, though non-circular motions exist.
AI.conclusion: REBELS-25 hosts a dusty, chemically enriched, and dynamically cold ISM already in place at z=7.31, supporting the early assembly of mature disc-like galaxies during the reionisation epoch.

title: Accretion Disk Sizes and Temperature Profiles in Lensed Quasars: NIR Microlensing Challenges Thin Disk Theory
comment: This is the Author Accepted Manuscript of an article published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The original publication will be available at A&A
summary: Microlensing and reverberation mapping measurements of quasar accretion disk sizes and temperature gradients disagree with thin disk theory predictions. Previous microlensing results rely on heterogeneous wavelength coverage -primarily UV broad emission lines (BELs) from small samples -probing the disk only out to a typical radius of $\lesssim$5 light days on average. We use microlensing estimates from an homogeneous sample of near-infrared (NIR) observations of lensed quasars (21 image-pairs from 7 lens systems) to extend disk size measurements out to 14 light days. This analysis leverages narrow emission lines (NELs), which provide a more reliable microlensing-free baseline than BEL cores. We derive Bayesian accretion disk size estimates that reproduce the observed microlensing magnifications, as simulated from magnification maps. NEL-based sizes yield a logarithmic slope of $p=0.68\pm0.23$, consistent with prior estimates corresponding to inner disk regions ($r \lesssim$5 light days). Using a new homogeneous NIR dataset that allows us to reach radial distances of up to 14 light days, we find that accretion disks in these previously unexplored regions are also larger and exhibit steeper temperature gradients than thin disk theory predicts. The increased precision allows us to reject the theoretical logarithmic slope $p=4/3$ at the 98\% confidence level. Any hypothesis invoking BLR contamination to explain this discrepancy must account for how such contamination modulates the underlying accretion disk such that the combination of both results in a power law with logarithmic slope $p=0.68\pm0.23$ across a broad wavelength baseline spanning from $\sim$X-Ray to $\sim 5000$Å.

title: Probing the Properties of Neutral Clouds in the Vicinity of the Local Bubble: Linking three-dimensional Dust with Neutral Hydrogen Absorption
comment: Accepted for publication in the Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia (PASA); 18 pages, 10 figures (two in appendix)
summary: The Local Bubble (LB) contains significant internal structure, with many interstellar clouds lying within or on its walls. By observing time variability of atomic neutral hydrogen (HI) absorption profiles in the direction of pulsars, it was suggested that some of the HI structures exhibit variations in optical depth representative of the tiny scale atomic structure (TSAS). However, the exact location of these structures has not been known and understanding their origin in the framework of LB formation and evolution has been impossible. We use three-dimensional dust maps to extract density profiles of the hydrogen volume density along the line-of-sight (LOS) to four selected pulsars. We attempt to correlate individual density components with the Gaussian components of the HI absorption spectra, revealing the TSAS towards B1929+10 likely lies outside of the LB. Comparing column density images integrated over the entire LOS and over sub-volumes of the 3D dust maps show a mixture of diffuse and clumpy structure. Using estimates of the mean HI volume density and maximum total neutral hydrogen density along the LOS, we place upper and lower limits on ionisation fraction and thermal pressure, respectively, to characterise the properties of the local ISM towards each pulsar. Our method of using HI absorption data in conjunction with three-dimensional dust data holds potential for broader applications, especially to validate the structures and properties of dust clouds in the LB and beyond.
